issues.description: Field StockIngredient.price has inconsistent types across artifacts. The problem statement UML (class StockIngredient) declares price as int and shows a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int). The template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java in the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY) declares price as double and has a constructor StockIngredient(String, double, int) with getPrice() returning double. The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java in the SOLUTION_REPOSITORY) declares price as int and uses an int-typed constructor and getter. This mismatch can confuse students about which numeric type to use when implementing SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice and may lead to inconsistent signatures and incorrect arithmetic expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the numeric type of StockIngredient.price consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Preferred fix: update the template StockIngredient to use int for the price field, change the constructor parameter to int, and change getPrice() to return int so it matches the UML and the solution implementation. Alternatively, if fractional prices are intended, update the UML/problem statement and the solution to use double everywhere. Ensure SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice use the same numeric type as StockIngredient.getPrice().
